question: Large bowel obstruction in an adult should be managed as colorectal carcinoma until proven otherwise, even if there is a history of previous diverticular disease that could explain the presentation.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This is true. Colorectal carcinoma accounts for ~60% of large bowel obstructions in adults. Attributing obstruction to diverticular disease without exclusion of malignancy is a dangerous error that delays diagnosis.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. Colorectal carcinoma is the most common cause of large bowel obstruction in adults. The clinical pearl: never be reassured by a history of diverticular disease — carcinoma must be excluded with contrast enema or CT colonography before attributing the obstruction to diverticulitis.
